newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Brunei plans US$1 bln refinery and chemicals plant.
newsitem.headline: Brunei plans US$1 bln refinery and chemicals plant.

text.p: Taiwan monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it was joining Japan's Kanematsu Corp and the Brunei government to build a US$1 billion refinery and petrochemical complex in Brunei.
Taiwan officials said the project would include a 60,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) refinery to process Brunei crude oil into oil products.
The complex would include an aromatics plant to produce and export 420,000 tonnes of paraxylene a year and 200,000 tonnes of benzene a year.

Paraxylene is used to manufacture purified terepthalic acid (PTA), a key component in polyester production, while benzene is used to make styrene monomer, a feedstock for making plastics and synthetic rubber.
The plan represents another move by the oil-rich sultanate to expand its energy sector away from reliance on crude production.
Brunei produces 165,000 bpd of crude oil, most of which is exported. It has a small 9,000-bpd refinery serving its population of 270,000.
In May, Brunei's Oil and Gas Agency signed a letter of intent to build a 160,000-bpd refinery at a cost of $1.5 billion with state-owned German engineering group IAB.
In the latest venture for Brunei, Chinese Petroleum officials said the company's chairman, Lee Shu-chiu, would travel to Brunei to sign a memorandum of understanding next Wednesday with its partners.
A detailed feasibility study would then be made over the next 18 months before the project would go ahead.
The partners share of the project would be determined about half way through the feasibility study, they said.
The plant would be geared to supplying the Southeast Asian market.
"The Brunei's project is aiming to supply its nearby countries," a senior Chinese Petroleum executive said. "Taiwan and Japan are also possible if prices are competitive."
"Chinese Petroleum will manage the operation with Brunei government's promise of stable crude supplies," he said. "Kanematsu, as a major trading company, can market the products."
Chinese Petroleum already produces 400,000 tonnes of paraxylene and 500,000 tonnes of benzene a year to serve the Taiwanese market.

Analysts estimate that Asia will increasingly rely on imports of oil products for several years, leaving room for new suppliers. Current imports are around 1.7 million bpd but that will rise to more than 2.0 million bpd by 2000, they say.
Demand for paraxylene and benzene are expected to also grow strongly in Asia, especially eastern Asia in the next 10 years, so that imports will be needed.
However, global pressures might act to push prices of the petrochemicals down, especially for paraxylene.
Chinese Petroleum officials declined to make forecasts now, but said a detailed feasibility study would also include the market potential and profitability.
Chinese Petroleum said its project with Kanematsu was not related to the German project.
--Taipei Newsroom (+8862 508 0815)
